title: Completeness tested by the walking-isomorphism restriction
statement:
Use homotopy Segal spaces and their homotopy categories $hX$ from [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence], and bisimplicial sets, vertical Reedy fibrancy and division notation from [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus]. Let $\mathcal J$ be the ordinary groupoid with objects $0,1$ and exactly one morphism between each ordered pair, and let $J=N\mathcal J$ be its ordinary nerve. Let $u_0:\Delta^0\hookrightarrow J$ select $0$. For every vertically Reedy fibrant homotopy Segal space $X$, completeness, meaning that $s_0:X_0\to X_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence, is equivalent to the assertion that endpoint restriction
$$u_0\backslash X:J\backslash X\longrightarrow\Delta^0\backslash X=X_0$$
is a trivial Kan fibration. Here $X_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq X_1$ is the union of components representing isomorphisms in $hX$, and trivial Kan fibration has the meaning of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper].

source.place: Lemma 4.2; comparison of the completeness convention with s_0:X_0 to X_eq from Rezk, https://arxiv.org/html/math/9811037, Theorem 6.2 and Proposition 6.4. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-homotopy result. Read online 2026-10-17; archive WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-reedy-homotopy-segal-comparison] to the given vertically Reedy fibrant homotopy Segal space $X$. It makes $X$ a Reedy fibrant Segal space in the strict-product convention, and identifies its strict-fiber homotopy category with the given $hX$ by the identity on objects and constant-path maps on arrows. Therefore the union $X_{\mathrm{eq}}\subseteq X_1$ and the degeneracy $s_0$ in the assertion agree with those in [lem-coef-segal-equivalence-classifier]. No completeness is used in this comparison.

source.place: Sections 4.1 and 5.1–5.5: comparison with the path-model convention before Theorem 6.2

proof.text: Let $t:J\to\Delta^0$ be the collapse, let $a:\Delta^1\to J$ be the edge $0\to1$, and set $A=J\backslash X$, $c=t\backslash X:X_0\to A$ and $p=u_0\backslash X:A\to X_0$. The division definition gives, in inner degree $q$, $A_q=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{ss}}(J\boxtimes\Delta^q,X)$. This is exactly $((X^E)_0)_q$ in [lem-coef-segal-equivalence-classifier]: its $E$ is $J$ made discrete in the inner direction, $F(0)$ is terminal, and $c\Delta^q=*\boxtimes\Delta^q$. The classifier applies by step 1 and supplies a weak homotopy equivalence $\epsilon:A\to X_{\mathrm{eq}}$ induced by $a$, with the exact identity $\epsilon c=s_0$.

source.place: Theorem 6.2, with the collapse and edge maps of Section 6

proof.text: Since $\epsilon$ is a weak homotopy equivalence and $\epsilon c=s_0$, two-out-of-three gives $s_0$ a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if $c$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Thus completeness defined by $s_0:X_0\to X_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is equivalent to the collapse-restriction condition used in Joyal–Tierney Lemma 4.2.

We have $tu_0=\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0}$, so contravariance of the division construction gives $pc=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}$ exactly. The identity is a weak homotopy equivalence; two-out-of-three therefore says that $c$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if $p$ is one. Together with step 3, completeness is equivalent to $p$ being a weak homotopy equivalence.

Finally $u_0:\Delta^0\hookrightarrow J$ is a monomorphism: in every degree it selects the simplex all of whose vertices are $0$. Vertical Reedy fibrancy and [lem-coef-bisimplicial-reedy-division-calculus] make $p=u_0\backslash X$ a Kan fibration, without assuming completeness. In the Kan model structure of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], a trivial fibration means a fibration which is also a weak homotopy equivalence, as stipulated in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Consequently $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence exactly when it is a trivial Kan fibration. Step 4 now proves both implications of the assertion.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 4.2, expanded with Rezk Theorem 6.2/Proposition 6.4 and the strict/path convention comparison; sources read online, archival copies WANTED.
